title: Mean annual biomass yield under roadside verge management regimes
source_table_or_section: Publisher abstract; only the three abstract-level aggregate means are transcribed
observation_period: 2013–2014; source-reported mean across the two years
license_status: No open reuse license identified for the journal article; metadata and aggregate factual values only, with DOI attribution.
scope: Three aggregate annual dry-matter yield means for repeated mulching, four-cut harvest, and two-cut harvest of urban roadside-verge grass.
method_context: Urban sites managed in 2013–2014; source abstract states 4 cuts for anaerobic digestion, 2 cuts for IFBB, and 8× mulching as reference. This file transcribes only the abstract's three mean annual yields, not the fuller year/site spread available in the article.
units_and_conversion: Source-reported t dry matter per hectare per year; no conversion applied.
uncertainty: No uncertainty statistics included in the abstract-level extraction. Site-/year-/replicate-level variability is not available in this file.
limitations: Kassel urban roadside grass is a European analogue, not Dutch roadside-grass evidence.
The values are biomass yields under study management regimes, not captured, accessible, contracted, or delivered feedstock.
Do not infer collection efficiency, seasonal monthly supply, or cumulative annual regrowth from these aggregate means.
Reference-only; no GreenHub runtime defaults or Pareto scenario inputs are changed.
applicability: Useful external comparison for how cutting frequency relates to annual roadside biomass yield; insufficient as a Dutch availability factor without local site and management validation.
